title: The fridge with no compressor
hook: No compressor, no refrigerant, no moving parts: just water, a vacuum and a mineral.

source.title: <the video's title>
source.transcript_file: <path to the transcript in the ingesting project>
source.note: EXAMPLE CARD. The numbers below are textbook values marked 'standard' or 'estimate' so the pattern is complete; a real card replaces them with what the video says, as 'claimed' numbers with timestamps.

summary: A molecular sieve is a zeolite: a mineral full of pores exactly the size of a water molecule. Put one in a sealed, air-free vessel beside a pan of water and it pulls the water's vapour in so hard that the water boils at room temperature, and boiling water gets cold. That is a refrigerator. When the zeolite is full, heat it and it gives the water back, ready to do it again.

beats.title: Water boils cold
beats.promise: Take the air away and water boils at room temperature.
beats.narration: Seal water in a vessel with the air pumped out and it boils at room temperature. Boiling takes heat, and it takes it from the water, so the water gets cold: every kilogram that boils off carries away {latent_kj_kg} kilojoules. The only trick is to keep taking the vapour away, and that is the zeolite's job.

beats.title: One bed, one day
beats.promise: How much cold a bed of zeolite holds.
beats.narration: A bed of {bed_kg} kilograms soaks up about {water_per_cycle_kg} kilograms of water before it is full. Boiling that much water away pulls {cooling_per_cycle_kwh} kilowatt hours of heat out of whatever the cold side touches.

beats.title: The sun resets it
beats.narration: When the bed is full, heat it to about {regen_c} degrees and it gives its water back, ready to go again. A solar collector does that. The price is heat: every day of cooling needs {heat_needed_kwh} kilowatt hours of it, because the cycle returns only {cop_thermal} of cold for each unit of heat.

dome_fit.title: Where it fits the dome
dome_fit.promise: The seam module's desiccant drawer, grown up.
dome_fit.narration: In the dome this is the seam module's desiccant cartridge, grown up. The three-way gate already sends the channel's air through a silica drawer that comes out and goes in an oven. A zeolite bed pulls harder, gives its water back to the sun instead, and makes cold while it works. Run once a day it gathers {water_per_year_gal} gallons of water a year, {vs_peltier} times what the seam's thermoelectric plates condense.

limits.narration: It is a daily batch, not an air conditioner: spread over the day it cools about {cooling_avg_w} watts on average, a fraction of what a small window unit moves.
And the heat has to come from somewhere: about {collector_m2} square metres of collector in good sun, on a dome whose whole shell is {dome_shell_sqft} square feet.
